newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania MPs replace privatisation agency managers.
newsitem.headline: Romania MPs replace privatisation agency managers.

text.p: Romania's lower house of parliament has replaced its three representatives on the administration board of the country's main privatisation agency, in a move slammed by the leftist opposition.

"The standing bureau of the Chamber of Deputies decided late on Thursday to replace its representatives to the State Ownership Fund (FPS) at the end of heated debates," Ovidiu Marian from the Chamber's press office said on Friday.
Seven of the Chamber's 13 standing bureau members voted in favour of the replacement after the opposition walked out in protest over the move, which it called "political cleansing".

Centrists who dominate parliament after last November's elections replaced the three FPS board members, which had been appointed by the former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) of ex-president Ion Iliescu.
The new centrist coalition government has pledged to speed up privatisation as part of its free-market reform package.

"The new government is entitled to pursue its own policy and it cannot do it as long as the FPS is dominated by the former ruling party," Chamber of Deputies speaker Ion Diaconescu told a local newspaper.
The FPS, which has been handling the bulk of privatisation since 1992, has been accused of stalling the sale of equity in some 6,500 state-companies in its administration.
Its 17-strong board includes three members from the Chamber and the upper Senate each, five from the presidency and the government each, plus the privatisation state secretary.
Under the law, FPS board members can be replaced before the end of their five-year mandate. The current board was appointed in June 1992.

The move follows local media reports that the FPS is put under legal scrutiny over alleged privatisation irregularities, by undervaluing the capital of some of the 3,000 companies that were put into private hands so far.
The FPS had no immediate reaction to the new appointments or to the allegations of irregularities. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
